label: Boyd allows apparent rational-supervenience failures and offers defeasible explanations
paraphrase: Boyd acknowledges apparent failures of rational supervenience in some actual and many counterfactual cases. He proposes that nearly all are cases of unrecognized failure of bivalence and that the remainder can receive realist explanations by innocent shortcomings of methodology or theoretical understanding. These are his explanatory proposals, not a demonstrated exhaustive diagnosis or a denial of determinate counterexamples in principle.
